body.estimand_functional: Put \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\) and let \(b_n=n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) for \(d\leq4t\), while \(b_n=n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) for \(d>4t\).  The proved all-regime statement is \(c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cb_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  On the proved no-penalty subregion \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\), \(\rho_n^*\asymp\rho_{n,e}^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\), with no logarithm at \(d=4\gamma\).  No independently derived repaired lower and upper maps have yet been proved equivalent.  The complete all-regime frontier, its unresolved transition logarithms, and the necessary direction of the known-propensity comparison therefore remain open; no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

sampling_model.design: Project-specific strengthening: \(X\) is known to be exactly uniform on the entire cube \([0,1]^d\), not merely to have a bounded density or to be uniform on a support with holes.
sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed observed margins of a law in \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A\) has unknown propensity \(e\) under the observational experiment; the comparison experiment supplies the exact function \(e_P\) to the test.
sampling_model.outcome: Observed and potential outcomes are binary.  The pointwise boxes \(m_0,m_1\in[1/4,3/4]\) are project-specific fixed interior regression margins on the canonical continuous representatives.
sampling_model.overlap: The project-specific numerical overlap box is \(e(x)\in[1/4,3/4]\) for every \(x\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator and no nuisance convergence rate is part of the class; all tuning is a deterministic function of \(n,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a pointwise CATE-estimation minimax rate in a larger model with a merely bounded covariate density and real outcomes; Section 3.1 supplies localized fuzzy-hypothesis and Hellinger machinery.  Its binary lower submodel uses a density uniform on an \(n\)-dependent support-with-holes \(S_{h,k}\), so that lower bound does not transfer downward to the present exact full-cube uniform-design subclass.
Theorems 4 and 6 give fixed-alternative consistency and a local weak limit for quantitative homogeneity tests over structured rule classes under the paper's nuisance conditions.

Theorems 1--2 establish asymptotic normality for propensity-reweighted pairwise and multisample adjusted \(U\)-statistics under consistent propensity estimation, independent stratum samples, stable positive sample fractions, and pointwise overlap.

Section 3 derives joint asymptotic normality and Gaussian-simulation calibration for multisample \(U\)-statistics testing equality of additive treatment effects across a fixed collection of mutually independent prespecified strata.

Theorem 6 gives asymptotic level, fixed-alternative consistency, and nontrivial \(n^{-1/2}\)-local power for a multiplier-bootstrap test of homogeneous restricted CATE with possibly right-censored duration outcomes.

Section 4 gives a conservative finite-sample-valid Fisher randomization test for the sharp null of one unknown constant individual treatment effect by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over a confidence set for that nuisance effect.

The main martingale-transformation results give asymptotic level for a permutation test of a constant marginal-distribution shift with an estimated nuisance shift, retaining exact level only for the more restrictive sharp null.
Theorems 3 and 7 give asymptotic chi-square tests of equality of finitely many score-defined group average treatment effects under complete randomization, with sample splitting or cross-fitting.

Theorems 4.1 and 5.2 give matching nonasymptotic binned conditional-independence radii for fixed discrete responses and a continuous conditioner under total-variation smoothness, a different null manifold and separation metric from constant CATE.

Theorems 6 and 7 give null validity and spline minimax power for projected conditional covariance under common smoothness and nondegeneracy restrictions, rather than a fixed-sample three-smoothness CATE radius.

Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 characterize bias, variance, and optimal separate wavelet resolutions for estimation of a signed expected conditional covariance functional; they guide nuisance resolution but do not test an unknown constant CATE.
The main minimax theorems derive sharp heteroskedasticity-detection rates using a squared first-difference proxy under a rough unknown mean.
Theorem 1 gives asymptotic normality and type-I error control for an intra-fold split CATE-variance statistic under explicit nuisance learner-rate conditions.
The paper proves that the propensity score is ancillary for semiparametrically efficient estimation of the regular average treatment effect under ignorability.
Theorems 3.3 and 3.4 give asymptotic null validity and consistency against smooth local sieve alternatives for the null that the conditional average treatment effect is constant.

The paper develops \(L_1\)-type tests based on uniformly consistent nonparametric kernel estimators for conditional treatment-effect restrictions and proves asymptotically correct size, fixed-alternative consistency, and power against some local alternatives.
Section 1 records the classical nonadaptive Hölder goodness-of-fit boundary, and the paper establishes the iterated-logarithmic price of adaptation in wavelet testing.

body.tldr: The proved result remains an honest all-regime bracket for the fixed-sample observational critical radius, together with the known-propensity benchmark and a matched no-penalty subregion.  With \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), the radius lies between \(n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\) and the explicit single-scale rate \(n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) for \(d\leq4t\), or \(n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) for \(d>4t\).  If \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\), both sides equal the known-propensity order.  The exact full-cube uniform design and fixed binary-regression margins are project-specific strengthenings; KBRW supplies only localized fuzzy-hypothesis methodology.  At the revised rough stress separation, the restored \(2+1\) projection is controlled, but an exact \(2+3\) fifth canonical projection has squared-likelihood scale \(\epsilon^{16}n^{1/5}\).  Thus this four-atom chi-square route fails, the complete frontier remains open, and no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

project_justification.gap: Existing homogeneity tests provide asymptotic validity, fixed-direction power, or finite-stratum comparisons, while existing minimax work concerns different null geometries, metrics, or pointwise CATE estimation.  On this project-specific binary exact-uniform class, the unresolved object is a matching fixed-sample lower and upper detection map across all three Hölder indices and all occupancy regimes.  The current likelihood audit shows that controlling the same-fine, \(2+1\), and nominal fourth-order terms does not control every higher connected macro--fine cluster.
project_justification.niche: The live mathematical niche is the likelihood-level interaction among an unknown constant-effect null, separate propensity and baseline roughness, macro-scale CATE variation, and repeated fine-cell collisions.  A sharp result must preserve exact uniform design, keep every null-prior component homogeneous, prove a direct finite-sample comparison, and pair it with an omnibus sparse-occupancy test on the identical class.
project_justification.fill: The established contribution supplies an explicit total single-scale fourth-order test, the all-regime bracket, the known-propensity benchmark, and a matched no-penalty subregion.  This round restores the exact \(2+1\) calculation, verifies it is only \(O(\epsilon^4)\) at \(n^{-3/10}\), and derives the previously uncharged \(2+3\) fifth canonical projection and its divergent squared-likelihood contribution.  That is a construction-specific diagnostic and a precise specification for the repaired converse, not a solution of the all-regime frontier.

body.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 is a method donor, not the source of the present exact class.  Its Theorem 1 permits a merely bounded covariate density and real outcomes, while its binary lower submodel is uniform on an \(n\)-dependent support-with-holes \(S_{h,k}\).  Because a converse on a larger class does not transfer downward to this exact full-cube uniform-design subclass, only the localized fuzzy-hypothesis and Hellinger architecture of Section 3.1 is imported here; the exact-uniform binary margins and every new likelihood calculation must be proved afresh.  NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 gives collision-sensitive nonasymptotic conditional-independence tests under total-variation smoothness, but its null manifold and metric differ from unknown-constant CATE.  LundborgKimShahSamworth2024, corresponding to PCM arXiv:2211.02039, gives projected-conditional-covariance validity and spline power under its own common-smoothness and nondegeneracy conditions, not a uniform fixed-sample radius on this three-index causal class.  DukesStensrudBrioschiHudson2026, arXiv:2410.00985v4, studies structured-rule homogeneity through asymptotic size, fixed power, and local weak limits under supplied nuisance conditions.  McGrathMukherjee2026, arXiv:2212.14857v5, derives separate nuisance resolutions for estimating a signed expected conditional covariance, which informs tuning but does not solve constant-CATE testing.  KBRW's pointwise estimation elbow, NBW's conditional-independence radius, PCM's projection test, Dukes et al.'s rule-class procedure, and McGrath--Mukherjee's estimation functional therefore do not supply the missing identical-class converse or omnibus test.  The remaining direct CATE-homogeneity predecessors in the comparator table are asymptotic, finite-stratum, score-group, distribution-shift, or sharp unit-level procedures; none provides the requested all-regime fixed-sample minimax frontier.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The frozen mixture envelope is invalid as a universal converse handle, and the frozen testing envelope is not sharp; both remain regression diagnostics.  For the bounded nested four-atom repair, every null component has constant CATE and all class-side and one-observation checks hold.  At \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), \(h\asymp\delta^5\), \(H\asymp\delta\), and \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\), the restored \(2+1\) contribution is \(\Theta(\epsilon^{10})\), hence controlled.  However, the exact \(2+3\) fifth canonical projection is \(\delta^4\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\kappa_4\kappa_5\), and its squared-likelihood contribution is at least \(c_b(n)_5hH^3\delta^8\asymp c_b\epsilon^{16}n^{1/5}\).  This disproves an \(O(\epsilon^4)\) support-controlled chi-square remainder for that prior.  Chi-square divergence alone does not exclude a direct Hellinger bound, so a different prior, a further cancellation, or a genuinely direct Hellinger comparison is still needed, as are the upper alternative dichotomy and sparse-occupancy concentration theorem.
body.honest_scope: The causal estimand remains the centered \(L^2\) norm of the CATE, and the statistical class remains the original project-specific binary exact-full-cube-uniform Hölder class with fixed overlap and interior margins.  The known-propensity rate is a comparator and carries no novelty claim.  The proved observational content is the all-regime bracket and the sufficient no-penalty region; smoothness adaptation is not claimed.  The restored \(2+1\) and new \(2+3\) calculations diagnose one prescribed four-atom prior and do not prove that every null-supported prior pays the same term.  KBRW is used only for methodological architecture, and its larger-model lower bound is not asserted on this subclass.  The complete rough-nuisance frontier, transition logarithms outside the proved region, and the necessary-and-sufficient propensity-value frontier remain open.  No conclusion certifies a fitted forest, and non-rejection is not evidence that the CATE is constant.
